東醫寶鑑雜病篇卷之二十

朝鮮總督府圖書館印

御醫忠勤貞亮扈聖功臣崇祿大夫陽平君臣許浚奉教撰

婦人

求嗣

作人則或痛或行則後血氣亦爭作不能成紫或黑或求必子或求前子之後或多先調經或毎見行婦

安經交則合男惟神足待子宮是以慾道而少調經或毎調行不要不

則雖克陰不多虛而抑不多動心能為上策道而慾念人寡不

盖存神養時雖遇男動不令火燃節亦精而不宜多宜多宜補而男子多精以微慾而靜

成矣男子温腎九疏弱陽而精充多宜時補而合一歲用微弱而靜

故而丹續服為温腎九清給于衛羸弱宮九薄男子固脉健弱陽宜

被而動微陽宜王鑰営給于盒斯九起石宮盒斯九女宜

朝鮮總督府南部韓本

貢737
translation:
Dongui Bogam: Miscellaneous Diseases Section, Volume 20

[Stamp: Joseon Government-General Library Seal]

Composed by royal physician Heo Jun, holder of the titles Loyal, Diligent, Upright, and Bright, Merit Subject of the Hoseong Order, Grand Master of Illustrious Prosperity, Duke of Yangpyeong, by royal command.

Women's Disorders

Seeking Heirs

When a woman has her period, there may be pain or flow, and afterward blood and qi contend with one another, so that conception cannot occur — whether the discharge is purple or black. Whether one seeks a son first or seeks a child after, the primary approach is always to regulate the menstrual cycle. Each time menstruation occurs, one must regulate it.

To harmonize the menstrual channels, when husband and wife unite, the spirit must be calm and the seed chamber properly prepared; desire must follow its proper course, with little distraction, and the channels must be regulated each month.

Although yin deficiency is present, one must not overly suppress it; the mind must not be disturbed. The best strategy is to follow the proper path and minimize excessive desire.

One must preserve the spirit and nourish it in due time. Even when the husband stirs arousal, one must not let the fire blaze up; the vital essence must be conserved and not squandered. It is appropriate to supplement, and the man must have abundant essence with minimal desire and a calm mind.

This is how conception is achieved. For the man, Warm the Kidneys Pill (溫腎丸) and similar remedies nourish and strengthen yang and replenish essence. These should be taken in due time to supplement. Use them in combination once a year with calming and gentle preparations.

Therefore, taking Warm the Kidneys Pill continuously will warm the kidneys, clear and supply the palace, and strengthen the weak. For men, use formulas to consolidate the pulse and strengthen yang.

For general use: Yuwang Key Formula, Yingying Formula, Heshi Formula, Shigong Formula, and for women, similar formulas are appropriate.

[Stamp: Joseon Government-General, Southern Section, Korean Edition]

驅濕宜合養血行濕烺岐南閟入香瘦宮附黃苓肥盛
疾防腥冒咋活嗽或門宮養宜行濕烺岐南閟半夏川芎滑石盛
癰末並調之相婦性多女惡行者

脈法

瘛令生精亦清尺魚際脈滑令如珠運虛極○若見微弱而滑無力○女精氣好

尺求調偏旺之尺陰專貴福於尺○惟沉右尺偏旨易為火動好色○微滋左

癰重宮顏血美俱侯不福宜薄不肥可满知宮太

和末者調之易婦撿氧未行性完姑然盛之月水婦不匀多相貌惡行者也

也嗛令
translation:
Methods for Examining Women (相女法)

Women who have no children — in many cases this is due to insufficiency of essence and the need to regulate and nourish the blood. It is appropriate to use [various formulas] to nourish the blood, regulate menstruation, warm the uterus, and supplement yang. When a woman conceives but cannot carry the child to term due to constitutional weakness, [appropriate medicines] should be administered.

[Various medicinal formulas and herbs are indicated for conditions such as:] Driving out dampness, nourishing the blood, warming the uterus, dispelling stagnation. Herbs such as Pinellia (半夏), Ligusticum (川芎), Talcum (滑石), Phellodendron (黃苓), and others are used accordingly.

Conditions of phlegm, food stagnation, and obstruction of the uterus causing irregular menstruation and poor constitution in women are also addressed.

Pulse Methods (脈法)

When the pulse at the chi (尺) position is slippery and rolling like beads, this indicates the essence and spirit are present. When the pulse is deep and faint or weak without strength, this is a sign of deficiency. If the right chi pulse is deep and the left is slightly slippery, this tends toward excessive desires and poor temperament.

When the palace [uterine] pulse is full and the blood is plentiful and the physique is good, fertility is favorable. When the pulse is thin, irregular, and the physical appearance and character are poor, conception is difficult.

translation:
Guben Jianyang Dan (Pill to Strengthen the Foundation and Invigorate Yang)

Many people who are without children are so because of deficiency of essence and blood, or because excessive sexual taxation has damaged them, causing insufficiency of kidney water. Though yang is vigorous, it cannot shoot directly into the uterus, hence no child is conceived.

One should especially attend to this matter. If the mother's blood is not interrupted and evil cold qi is expelled without heat, apply moxibustion. [Ingredients include:] Dioscorea (yam), washed and steamed in wine; Achyranthes (ox-knee), wine-washed and wine-prepared; Morinda root (Bajitian), stir-fried and cored; White silk [dodder seed?], 2 liang; Angelica root body, wine-washed and steamed; Cuscuta (dodder), stir-fried; Cistanche (Roucongrong), soaked in wine, washed; Eucommia bark, wine-fried until threads removed; Lycium (wolfberry), washed and fried — each 1 liang; Ginseng, salted and fried; Dang Gui (Angelica); Dioscorea, roasted; Eucommia; each ingredient rice-prepared.

Astragalus, longan, Alpinia, stir-fried; Deer antler, roasted; 1 liang each. Grind all ingredients into fine powder, form into honey pills. Take on an empty stomach with salt water or plain water.

Take 70 pills of Renshen Yuling [formula] again, adjusted with water to form pills.

For use: 4 liang, take with Asparagus root (Tianmen dong), dodder, Lycium, Dragon bone — 2 liang each.

Xusi Dan (Pill for Continuing Descendants)

Morinda (Bajitian), prepared Rehmannia, stir-fried; 4 liang; Asparagus root (Tianmen dong), dodder, Lycium, Dragon bone, Rubus (Fupengzi) — 2 liang each. Dioscorea, prepared Rehmannia, Angelica — 2 liang each; various ingredients 1 liang and a half; Dragon bone 7 qian; Phellodendron; Placenta hominis (Ziheche); Citrus peel; Oyster shell; Cnidium seed — half [qian]. White wood ginger, each 5 qian; Angelica, Asparagus, Rehmannia, roasted — 7 qian each; ground into fine powder, made into honey pills.

Take with warm wine or salt water. Take 100 pills each time on an empty stomach.

Wenshan Jiu (Kidney-Warming Pills)

[Contains:] Dodder, Angelica, Deer antler, Piper, Alpinia (Yizhi ren), Rehmannia, Lycium, Rehmannia raw, Fennel, Morinda (Bajitian) — each 2 liang, [with] Spirit [of the formula].

translation:
Warm the Womb Moschus Pill (煖宮麝斯九)

For women who cannot conceive, take this formula. Ingredients include: Magnolia bark (厚朴) 1 liang 2 qian half; Aconite (附子); Evodia (吳茱萸).

[Further ingredients at various quantities:] Ginseng (參), Saposhnikovia root (防風), Ampelopsis root (白蘞), Dried ginger (乾薑), White Poria (白茯苓), Honey (蜜), Adenophora root (沙參), Asarum (細辛), and others.

This pill is used to treat women who are barren and cannot conceive. It addresses conditions including red and white vaginal discharge (帶下), uterine bleeding (崩漏), and irregular menstruation. It regulates the heart and circulation, reduces swelling, and normalizes the menstrual cycle.

Additional ingredients include: Ligusticum (川芎), Red Halloysite (赤石脂), Gastrodia (豪本/藁本), Ginseng (人參), Moutan bark (丹皮), White Poria (白茯苓), Hematite or mineral astringent (石脂), and Cinnamon (桂).

This formula warms the uterus and is indicated for women who have difficulty conceiving due to cold and deficiency in the womb, with symptoms of menstrual irregularity, vaginal discharge, and related conditions. Pregnant women must not take it.

translation:
On Avoiding Inauspicious Times for Yin-Yang Union (Sexual Intercourse)

If one chooses the proper time to unite, there is nothing that will not come to fruition. From the moment a person begins life, it is blood [that is fundamental].

The sea [of vitality] begins to grow: on the first, second, and third days, the essence and spirit are said to be flourishing. The gate [of vitality] is open, and this governs the timing.

[Regarding conception:] The jade [essence] is thin; one must face forward on the first day — this is called the flourishing of the divine spirit. Those who do not seek a child should still follow the method of union with their spouse.

After the passing [of menstruation], on the first day, the essence and vitality are renewed. If one unites during the four seasons — spring, the jiǎ and yǐ days, the second month, through summer and the bǐng days — one may conceive.

For wind, rain, meetings under rainbows, fog, thunder, great cold, the bǐng-dīng days, great heat, lightning, and at new and full moon — these are all times to avoid union.

One must not engage in union inside Buddhist temples or shrines; if one does not follow proper method and timing, blessings and virtue will not accumulate.

If one follows the proper methods and the way of the household, virtue and blessings will flourish. If one does not follow proper guidance, calamities will follow, as sure as a needle's prick.

translation:
Nurturing the Fetus in the Tenth Month

During a woman's pregnancy, at the first and third months the foot lesser yin meridian nourishes; at the sixth month the yang brightness meridian nourishes; at the fourth and second months the foot lesser yin meridian nourishes; at the eighth month the hand greater yang meridian nourishes; these concern the fetal water and yang; at the ninth month various meridians nourish; therefore, in each month the yin nourishes through the greater yang meridian; those who begin nourishment at the fourth month use the greater yang foot and eighth month meridian nourishes.

For thirty days, the nourishing of the child activates the pulse; the child nourishes the hand and foot lesser yin and greater yang meridians; at ten months the child's heart and vital essence are cultivated.

Milk, essence, and vital energy flow through the meridians to nourish the fetus; the mother's blood and fine red blood circulate.

First Month

At the first month, the father's essence and the mother's menstrual regulation converge; the meridians open to nourish the fetus. The fetus is like a sphere of yellow color, like a single precious bead, quiet and still, gradually forming within the fluid sac.

The outer layer forms a wrapping of yellow and mixed colors; inside, the embryo gradually consolidates, round as a ball, resting quietly, the fluid sac enclosing it.

It then resembles a small pellet, like a pill, round; after seven days it transforms further, consolidating gradually.

During this time one should not overexert, should avoid emotional disturbance, and must refrain from excessive eating and drinking, so that the child may grow healthily through the year.

translation:
Seventh Month:
The Hand Taiyin Lung meridian nourishes the fetus; it is now able to move, and the essence begins to form the skin and flesh.

Eighth Month:
The Hand Taiyang Large Intestine meridian nourishes the fetus; it begins to receive and intake, completing the formation of the skin and flesh.

Ninth Month:
The Foot Shaoyin Kidney meridian nourishes the fetus; it begins to receive the essence of stone (mineral essence), enabling the body's organs to form and all pathways to connect.

Tenth Month:
The Foot Taiyang Bladder meridian nourishes the fetus; it receives the five organs' functions and brings birth.

Pulse During Pregnancy:
When the middle pulse waving is very strong it is called "turbulent water." If the Shaoyin pulse beats strongly in the hand and the Yang pulse is separate, this is called the Yin-chi moving pulse.

When pressing the pulse and it is not slippery or rapid, but when pressing hard it disperses — yet the rapid quality does not disappear — this indicates the fifth month of pregnancy. If all three positions of the pulse feel heavy under pressure and float under the hand, this indicates the eighth month, third position, and the pulse is heavy — because it is a Yang pulse, therefore the fetus is heavy.

[Further passages discuss pulse distinctions for pregnancy:] If the pulse of the lesser yin and greater yang are distinct and the chi (cubit) pulse moves, the woman is pregnant. If it is a full, rounded pulse in the hand indicating a son; if the pulse characteristics differ, other determinations are made. By the third month the yang pulse confirms the pregnancy.

When all five viscera are fully prepared and await their time, birth occurs naturally. The governing official oversees the six seasonal periods of life.

The Kidney meridian pulse at its node nourishes the fetus; beginning at the third month it receives the mineral essence, enabling the five organs to form, and activating movement in both the left and right hands.

translation:
The pulse that is sunken, upright, firm and forceful — when pressed it has no bowstring-like tautness; a tight pulse indicates pregnancy. A sunken and thin pulse indicates death. In the eighth month of pregnancy the pulse is six or seven [beats per breath].

Method for Examining the Fetus
If the qi is even, dispersed and relaxed, childbirth will be easy. A large, floating, relaxed, strong, bowstring, and tight pulse indicates pregnancy and a viable birth; a sunken and thin pulse indicates death. If a pregnant woman has heart vexation, alternating cold and heat, and her period has not come for three months, one suspects she is carrying two bodies — this is difficult to verify. [Use] Mugwort and Vinegar Decoction.

Miraculous Formula: Fetus-Examining Powder
Use true sparrow brain, two liang; Angelica root (whole), seven qian. Grind to a fine powder and take mixed with wine. If the fetus is present, the abdomen will stir and move. If it does not move, there is no fetus.

Mugwort and Vinegar Decoction
[Taken to] promote sensation downward; [if the woman] feels no effect, the abdomen will not respond; take again; if there is no great effect, use this formula decocted with safflower — if pregnancy is present, the vinegar cooking will cause pain; if no pregnancy, there will be no pain; take with salt.

Method for Distinguishing Male from Female
[Various methods follow:] Choose the right side — if the right breast is fuller and firmer, it is a male. If one turns back, it is female. A person who has left-side fullness — if the woman's left breast is firmer, it is a male. Like cotton — if round and full, it is female.

脈法
陰陽疾婦人偕人疾姙為男偏沉為女男左女右手偏大為男左右沉實為男俱手大偏沉男疾為男女二左沉實在以右男左右取左右男可為俱男浮疾為生女二沉實在男女浮大在右以女別生左以預訓女男

雙胎品胎
成男坤道成女夫乾坤陰陽之性精也左右陰陽道宮日乾道宮易日坤精勝之後亦主夫精濕之論也男一女者褚精澄勝之後分男女後一女者諸精濕之論也成女四玉日成男坤道必精束短之日後竟兌分後男成男
translation:
When a pregnant woman is resting in the upper position at the time shown in the diagram, and her husband calls out to her from beside her, if she turns her head to the left, it is a boy; if she turns her head to the right, it is a girl. When turning the head to the left, the blood and qi protect that side heavily. When she turns her head to the left, the blood protects and qi is heavy on the left, and the pulse on the left is rapid, indicating a male. The left pulse is large, indicating male. The pulse on the left follows it and flourishes on the left, so the pulse also follows and the left being rapid indicates male. If on the left, then the fetal pulse is flourishing on the left, and tends toward the left. By extension, the fetal pulse follows its position, so the right pulse also follows, meaning if the fetus is on the right, it is female, the pulse being rapid on the right indicates female. The fetus tends rightward. The fetal position buried on the right side: a female child from the right — this is the female. In the fourth month one can discern whether the companion is male or female, and so the method of determining: rapid on the right, the chi pulse indicates —

Pulse Diagnosis Methods:
Yin and yang rapid — in pregnant women, if both persons' pulses are rapid, it indicates male; if slanted and sunken, it indicates female. Male left, female right. If the hand pulse is slanted and large, it indicates male. If left and right are both sunken and full, it indicates male. If both hands are large and slanted-sunken, male rapid indicates male. For female, if the second position on the left is sunken and full, taking left and right, male left and right can both indicate male. Floating and rapid indicates the birth of a female. If the second position sunken and full: male and female floating large on the right — with the female differentiated by birth on the left.

Double Fetus / Special Fetal Presentations:
The way of Qian (Heaven) produces males; the way of Kun (Earth) produces females. The husband's Qian and Kun, yin and yang in nature are the essence. Left and right yin-yang palace: the Classic says the Qian palace, the Book of Changes says the Kun essence. When the husband's essence overcomes, afterward it governs. When the husband's essence is dominant and moist, the theory goes: one male then one female — Zhu's theory of essence clarity overcoming: after separation into male and female, one female — the various theories of essence moisture. Producing female: the four jade days produce male; the Kun way must have the essence condensed and shortened after which the transformation separates, afterward producing male.

text: 之道路也男女陰陽之儀撮家之也父精母血醫感而成形也精氣居右名物成其右曰瑩左精分吸男則於左精達右一主感兩岐之時陰之左一胎元此也居萬物此化血成陰胎其之肥乃血形成陽之為次日成陰矣形彩或時不精氣同感分吸男則左右精達一主感兩岐胎元乃血形成陽之為次女及形彩男也日成日精氣不同感分吸則胎者問女及形彩或時不精陰陽之為次成日下陽時有兩燥乾胎元也字胎此也則一陽建為次左一胎元此也居萬物此化血成陰胎其之肥乃血形成陽之為次三選若老者胎雖四不男日胎屬左同精氣有同感分吸或右則剛岐男則分吸左精右曰瑩名物成其精於右居此化血成陰胎其也血成形也精氣居右名物成其目而日感胎者胎屬六層胎右剛岐男則分吸左精右曰瑩名物成其精於右居此化血成陰胎其也乃血形成陽之為次父與老考父義日女胎本可寫世父與老考父義日女以女塞氣者寫為男也又可以女塞氣形而男也驟妻而二妻又形義也不可為分可三洗胎雖四不男日胎屬左同精氣有同感分吸則胎者夫也日陰之陽故者胎而有雙胎敵胎陰者而有感也則之陰分失氣男形彩或時不精陰陽之為次成日下時感也則之陰分失氣男形彩成胎宮騏精不時陽宮騏上陽有感兩岐之時陰之左一胎元此也女子宮血一系及男騏於其宮勝子生子於此精萬之坤无物也於此精萬之坤无物也之道路也男女陰陽之儀撮家之也父精母血醫感而成形也精氣居右名物成其右曰瑩左精分吸男則陰陽分時兩梁日因之陰分失氣男形彩女寫于吾之主而沒男形女子宮血一系及男騏於其宮勝子生子於此精萬之坤无物也氣陽分時時兩梁此岐日因之阴分失氣男形彩獨是氣而已或成日此也驟氣易于而形又義也騏女為陰而全夫形一則又可以女塞氣形而男也驟妻而二妻又形義也不同邪於日陰體獨見具遇男女為陰二為狀得陰日女一氣男以之女塞氣不可寫為男也又可以女塞氣形而二而妻又形義也不可為夫或又日下為遇男女體鷹而且赤而可而分可三洗胎雖四不男也有一阴則也為騏駿氣男女為陰而全夫形一則又可以女塞氣者是也不同邪於日陰體虛驟氣易于而成之形義又形而騏義也不可為分可三洗胎雖四不男日胎屬左同精氣有同感分吸者惠是者也不同邪於日陰體虛驟氣易于而成之形義又形義也
translation:
This text discusses the foundational principles of yin-yang theory as applied to human reproduction and fetal development in traditional Chinese/Korean medicine. The following is a faithful rendering of its content:

The path of the Dao: the ceremonial distinctions between male and female, yin and yang, are the foundation of the household. The father's essence (jing) and the mother's blood, stirred by the physician's understanding of sensation and response, unite to form the body. The essence-qi resides on the right; named substances complete it. The right is called "radiance" (ying). The left essence divides and is absorbed. If male, then on the left the essential qi meets, and the two branches of the womb-element are felt; the fetal origin thus arises. This is how blood and form become the yang. Women and the coloring of form — or at times when the essence is insufficient — the yin-yang sequence proceeds and the day of formation arrives.

When the essence-qi does not harmonize and the division of absorption differs, if the fetus belongs to the left with the same essence-qi having the same sensation and the right is firm, the male divides and absorbs from the left essence. The right is called "radiance." Named substances complete the essence; it resides on the right, where blood transforms into the yin fetal body and nourishes it. Blood then forms into yang as the next step.

Three selections: if the person is old, even though a fetus forms, a male may not result. The fetal attributes belong to the left; with the same essence-qi and same sensation, the fetus forms. The husband's role: the yin within the yang — thus the fetus may have twins; opposing the fetus in yin, if sensation is present, then the yin divides and the qi of the male form is lost. Form and coloring, or when essence is insufficient — the yin-yang sequence then proceeds.

The essence in the womb rises in yang; when both branches are felt, the left one of yin forms the fetal origin. The child is born in the womb; through essence and the ten-thousand things of the receptive (kun), without physical object, on this the essence of ten-thousand things of kun rests without object.

The path of the Dao: male and female, yin and yang — the ceremonial foundation of the household. The father's essence and mother's blood, stirred by medical understanding, unite to form shape. The essence-qi resides on the right; named substances complete it on the right, called "radiance." The left essence divides; if male is absorbed, the yin-yang divides in time between the two beams — the yin divides and the male's qi and form are lost. The female writes/gives form to the self's master without the male form.

The woman's womb-blood, one system connecting the male's qi to her womb, the child born — through the essence of ten-thousand things of kun, without physical object. The qi and yang divide in time; through the two beams and branches, the yin divides and the male's qi and form are lost, uniquely becoming qi — or it becomes so. The form also follows this reasoning.

They are not the same — heresy — on the day the yin body alone sees and meets male and female; as yin, the two together gain the yin, and the woman alone with qi cannot be written as male. Again, the woman may be filled with qi of form and thereby become male. If the wife and her two (forms) also follow this reasoning, it cannot be for dividing — one may do three cleansings; though a fetus forms four times, it may not result in male.

Summary: This passage deals with traditional theories of sex determination in the fetus, the role of yin-yang balance of parental essences, twin pregnancies, conditions under which female can transform to male, and the conditions of fetal formation according to classical Korean-Chinese medicine as recorded in the Dongui Bogam.

听乘陰陽相混無所為主氣不可輕重而不可屬故左右受

微於兩岐之間隨所得氣之沉澱實。丹生漢形成。二此男論不極造女精

悪阻

絶有其醫迓遣候者即一安月也加剉吐下社娘裏受之法朔便皆者
translation:
Method for Transforming a Female Fetus into a Male

When yin and yang are mixed together with no dominant force, the qi cannot be weighted lightly or heavily and cannot be assigned to one side; thus left and right receive [qi indiscriminately].

The subtle [qi] settles between the two diverging paths, following whichever qi is received, sinking and clarifying into substance. The cinnabar [elixir] produces the Han form [i.e., male form]. In both cases, the male discourse does not go to extremes in producing female essence.

A male produces a male; female life arises on the left and right. When the pulse on both sides is the same, it indicates a male student. At the beginning of the prescribed method, the essence flows and a male form is produced, changing accordingly.

At the time when [the woman] is pregnant, in the third month, the name is not yet fixed. From that day onward, she begins to take the fetal formulas; the blood and pulse [are observed]. Let it be known to the woman.

When she first perceives [the pregnancy], in the mao [period], having confirmed pregnancy, she must necessarily run to gather [the herbs] and place [them] under the pregnant woman, so that it becomes known — [even] a stallion cannot surpass this.

[Using] a bowstring [bound with] rhino horn — wrap it. The waist [is bound with] a male bow string.

Fill [to] three [units]; use realgar. During its peak, carry [this] at the woman's side. Take a bow and bind it. The head [is bound with] a male bow string. [Give this to] the husband.

The woman's seat, hands and feet, [with] geng/jia [days] noted — let the pregnant woman know. Place flowers on the mat, named "direct male" — do not let the woman know. [Then] the woman is overturned [i.e., the fetus is turned].

Fully satisfying [all requirements], press [the fetus]; let [the woman] know. Place grass under the pregnant woman's left seat cushion. Take [this from] the husband.

Aversion to food (Nausea/Morning Sickness — 悪阻):

Symptoms include inability to eat, absence of digestive fire, accumulation [of phlegm], retching, dislike of food, dizziness, aversion to eating — this is the condition. Take [the formula for the] woman.

Extreme cases require a physician to visit and attend. At one month, [the patient] vomits, and those below [in the household] receive [the treatment] according to the method — administered from the new moon onward, all [symptoms] should resolve.

translation:
Obstructed [pregnancy] sickness: its symptoms show a normal complexion and pulse, but the patient feels fullness and oppression in the chest and diaphragm, aversion to the smell of food, vomiting or retching, inability to keep down water, at times unable to bear up; Master Ye calls this alternating cold and heat.

Dizziness of the head and eyes; after eating, acid regurgitation from the stomach, aversion to food. In women, when the menses first cease and the pulse closes off at the uterus, when the fetal qi is flourishing, the middle will necessarily become aversive to foul smells.

Heart vexation and fullness in the middle; eating and drinking in excess, vomiting everything, improving day by day. The fetus being secure, the original qi having stagnated and water retained—

The obstruction: when there is much blood blocked, the flow of food and drink is obstructed; slight vomiting, dizziness and heaviness of the head and eyes, frequent nausea, the woman's nutritive blood nourishing the fetus, which flourishes; necessarily the essence-qi stirs and combines, water is retained.

Food and drink: urgent and excessive vomiting, or mild vomiting, dizziness, frequent nausea—named "inner chamber" obstruction. Food accumulates, the aversion qi has not yet dispersed, coughing, the pulse is closed at the uterus, the fetus flourishes, necessarily the center becomes aversive to foul odors.

Urgent panting: the bowel is obstructed, vomiting day after day, entering the gate closing off the pregnancy; if there is initial stoppage, the pulse is closed, the four limbs [suffer], blood nourishes the uterus and fetus, flourishing, necessarily combined, the essence-qi stirs, water is retained. The aversion does not contend, confused and dazed the fetus flourishes.

After eating, the stomach becomes aversive—by high command urgency, from this deeply there are two gains; illness, aversion to food, day by day it disperses; those who have postpartum [conditions] have the meaning of lochia-water—the fetus flourishes externally, muddled and confused.

The ancient recipe: by urgent command, chasing away the meaning; it is from this, deeply is two gains: illness, aversion to food, day by day dissolves; postpartum there is afterwards the lochia-water meaning, externally muddled and confused.

Heart-liver [formula] with fresh ginger, adding Atractylodes, with hot aconite; for those who eat and are heated daily; fat persons with much phlegm should all follow the previous [formula]; postpartum there is the meaning of lochia-water.

Powder of White Ginger with bamboo shavings added; long-term inability to take in water or gruel: second treatment. ○ On Chen's [formula for] obstructed pregnancy: phlegm with worry; old bamboo also has [uses].

For Banxia (pinellia) [syndrome] during the half-period; decoction for returning origin qi, weakness, unable to supplement; ○ during pregnancy, pinellia [for] vomiting, weeping and crying, [adding] much [medicine], also add Coptis and tangerine peel.

translation:
Two-Chen Decoction (Er Chen Tang)

In cases where a pregnant woman has nausea and cannot eat, this is because the fetus is unsettled. Although the pregnancy is stable, food cannot be taken and the woman grows thin and weak. This formula is used to cure such conditions. However, if one does not know this formula and discusses fetal movement and illness without using Pinellia (banxia), the fetus stirs and illness results. Use only these two ingredients — this formula cures the condition. But use only these two.

Shen-Ju Powder (Ginseng and Tangerine Peel Powder)

For treating this condition of nausea and vomiting before delivery — half a qian each. This illness is one of fetal unrest with vomiting of fluid, heart vexation, and the patient cannot take Ginseng. [Ingredients:] Tangerine peel, Bamboo shavings, Chicken egg [yolk], Citrus peel, Red [variety], Licorice root — one fen each.

Bai Zhu Powder (White Atractylodes Powder)

One qian each, chopped. For treating nausea and vomiting. One packet. Also named Shen-Ju-Zhu-Ru-Ji-Zi [Ginseng-Tangerine-Bamboo-Egg] Powder. Take daily, divided into two doses morning and evening. White Atractylodes five qian. Chop the ingredients on the right. Five qian.

Bao Sheng Tang (Life-Preserving Decoction)

When a woman's pulse in all positions indicates pregnancy — this is the pulse of a pregnant woman. When a woman's monthly period stops and her body has no illness yet seems ill, with a deep, large pulse in all six positions — this indicates pregnancy.

[Preparation:] Decoct in water with five slices [of ginger], take as a dose. Add five fen of cloves, one qian two fen of [another ingredient], five fen of licorice. Chop the right-side ingredients.

translation:
One Formula

Prohibitions and Taboos During Pregnancy

[Query regarding a pregnant woman of two months who has severe vomiting, facial flushing, and dizziness: use ginseng, atractylodes, Chuanxiong, tangerine peel, and poria to address the pregnancy. After taking Poria Decoction, the liver qi flows freely; then take nine green willow pills, take several doses of root decoction to tonify, and recovery will follow.]

It is advisable to take Poria Decoction, then take nine green willow pills, and further take root decoction for the abdomen, using ginseng and atractylodes in ten-pill doses; take several doses to tonify and recovery will follow.

[If one decocts and chews it in water, having received pregnancy, intercourse is taboo after the birth; after pregnancy, sharp objects, cutting instruments and striking must be avoided; such violations will injure the fetus.]

Dietary Prohibitions During Pregnancy

Eating horse meat causes the child to be born in a breech or awkward position and makes labor difficult. Eating dog meat causes the child to be born without a voice. Eating mule meat causes the child to be born without a voice and makes labor difficult. Eating chicken eggs and chicken meat [causes harm]. Eating crab combined with glutinous rice causes the child to be born in a transverse position. Eating raw sparrow meat causes the child to have many desires and to develop intestinal worms. Eating ginger and taro in excess or certain plant seeds [causes harm].

Dietary Prohibitions [General]

Eating overturned-nest mushrooms and chicken meat together causes the child to be sickly. Eating malt causes the fetal qi to be dispersed. Eating stove mushrooms causes the child to waste away. Eating catfish and malt causes the fetal qi to be dispersed, leading to sores. Eating mountain goat meat causes the child to develop spasms and convulsions. Eating various fish in general causes the child to develop pox and sores.

translation:
Prohibited Combinations of Medicinal Substances

The Verse Says:
Sulfur and arsenic must not be combined with dried lacquer and pine resin; male dragon flowers, chicken, clams, and toads; crab, fish, ox lacquer, Pinellia (summer), southern [herbs]; Aconite (tianxiong), wild kudzu, leech, water leech; and Croton seed (Badou), Aconite (wutou), monkshood (fuzi), centipede; [various combinations follow listing] ox gallstone horn, toad; armor, morning glory, safflower; crab claws are prohibited; [further incompatibilities listed with] sulfur, charcoal, dragon, phoenix; sacred leaven; garlic and tin; dried [herbs]; crab and orchid; large doses of crab and orchid; perilla, tin, armor, morning glory, safflower; horse silver root yam; chicken, chrysanthemum, taro, cinnamon, Chinese lovage; ginger, whole bile, gentian, astragalus; cattail, reed, earthworm, saltpeter; grapes, berries, peach kernel; fritillaria, coptis, goosefoot, ochre; tangerine peel, ox, peach, south; crab, fish, ox, pinellia; toad, salamander, dragon flower; sulfur, arsenite, dried lacquer, ox; parrot, dragon, chicken, clams, toad.

Methods for the Care of Pregnant Women

Large doses of rhinoceros horn; magnolia bark, warming [formula]; do not eat [certain foods]; do not take large doses or use moxibustion; do not drink to intoxication; do not overexert or bow the head; do not walk up stairs or climb heights when [conditions apply].

Do not cross险险 险 places or take large medicines when warming; do not overexert to the point of pain; do not sleep too much near the end of the month; do not bow the head at certain times; do not climb or walk up at certain times.

Restlessness of the Fetus

Fetal Leakage and Fetal Stirring

[Use] Ai (mugwort) Eight-Substance Decoction, stir-fried with sand [amomum], add [various herbs]; add and boil, take orally; this formula rescues [the patient]; fetal sounds [indicate] true fetal leakage and fetal stirring.

Decoction with added flavors: stir-fried amomum, aucklandia, cyperus, four substances blackened.

Decoction with terminalia: when fetal stirring is felt, add herbs; fetal turning with bleeding below; this condition belongs to the category of [deficiency]; blood alum has heat; fetal leakage, fetal stirring.

translation: In all cases where there is bleeding below, with fetal movement, abdominal pain, fetal leakage, fetal stirring, and membrane pain — these are distinguishing symptoms. One should clear heat, and in cases of fetal movement with deficiency of blood and qi, fetal leakage without membrane settling, one should self-administer cooked [preparations]. There are those who are harmed by blood, those harmed by excessive alcohol consumption, and those harmed by binding and restriction of the lower channels. Those harmed in the fetus cannot settle themselves, due to overexertion causing disease, or violating prohibitions. In mothers who cause illness and stirring, there are those who simply cannot treat the fetal disease well. In cases where the fetus is small and frequently descends, the uterus itself can expel the pregnancy — this is the case for pregnant women with internal hardness. Fang Qi Tang has wonderful merit; observe and know to add it for pregnant women, with alcohol-fried supplementing [herbs] and Huang [Qi]. For fetal leakage, the four appropriate supplementing formulas are: Sheng Jiao Tang, Bu Fang, and using Jiao Ai Tang — the fetal stirring引 leads to Jiao Ai [preparations]. Tang Bu San, Sheng San, Di Huang Sheng An Tai Jiao Ji Yao Fu Tai Ai Ai. Tang Dang Di An Tai Huang Bai Sheng Tang An Jiao An Tang Dong. Use She Lan Wan, San Xue, Ban Bai Song Sheng Tang Ji Ben Bai Huang. Bu Jiu Du Zai Tai Zhi Di Huang An Tai Huang Cha Yu Huang. Zhi Ke Tang: One treatment for fetal stirring and bleeding below — half dose, right Song, make one packet, decoct in water with E Jiao. Xiao Jiao Ai Tang: Treats four cases of fetal stirring with bleeding — make three packets, decoct in water with moxa. Jiao Ai Tang: Treats fetal stirring — one packet decocted in water with roasted licorice and moxa, one qian each, Sheng Di, one qian, Shi Ke, make one packet with Chuan Xiong and E Jiao.

Take twice daily. [Formula:]

Gelatin and Mugwort Decoction with Angelica (Jiao Ai Gui Tang):
Treats fetal stirring with abdominal pain and bleeding in the eighth or ninth month of pregnancy, as well as threatened miscarriage. Treats leaking of membranes with pain. Ingredients: processed rehmannia, angelica, ligusticum, white peony, mugwort leaf, cyperus (roasted). Take a pinch of each, decoct with water, cut and take on an empty stomach; add glutinous rice, atractylodes, cardamom, mugwort, ligusticum.

Treats fetal conditions. 1 qian each; for bleeding: ginseng, mulberry mistletoe, teasel root, processed rehmannia, 7 fen each. Cut and scrape, make one packet, decoct and take warm to stop bleeding.

Aconite, blood-moving herbs, mulberry mistletoe, teasel root, ligusticum, angelica. Cut and scrape, treat weakness, regulate [leaking and menstrual irregularities].

[Duzhong Continuation Pill]

Take for fetal restlessness and low back pain, to prevent miscarriage and calm desire. Make into pills the size of firmiana seeds with jujube flesh and powdered, dry-fried Duzhong (eucommia bark). Take with water.

Danggui Dihuang Decoction (Angelica and Rehmannia Decoction)
Two liang each. Grind into powder, mix with jujube flesh and form pills the size of firmiana seeds. Take with powdered dry-fried Duzhong decoction.

Antai San (Fetus-Calming Powder)

Antai Yin (Fetus-Calming Beverage)

Huangqin Tang (Scutellaria Decoction)

translation:
Internal Supplementing Pill

Treats deficiency of the Chong and Ren vessels, tonifies blood, and calms the fetus. Cooked rehmannia (地黃) 2 liang, Chinese angelica (當歸) 5 qian [1 liang]. Lightly dry-fry. Grind the above into powder. Form into honey pills the size of a parasol tree seed. Take on an empty stomach with warm wine.

Solitary Sage Powder

[Dosage:] 9 to 7 pills, 10 [times]. Treats cases where falling or injury has caused fetal stirring, changes in the abdomen, pain that is unbearable, and fetal contraction. Arsenic (砒石), dry-fried and peeled, ground into powder. For each contraction [take with] rice wine or yellow wine. If one feels internal abdominal pain, slowly fry over a low flame to calm the spirit and stop the pain. Take dissolved in water. If one feels internal abdominal pain at its extreme, to calm and contract the fetus, take arsenic powder each time for contraction.

Anemarrhena Pill

[Timing note.] Treats fetal conditions using rehmannia juice, two he, mixed and decocted, taken on an empty stomach. Form into honey pills the size of a parasol tree seed. For those who wish to deliver before the months are full, [take] when abdominal pain comes. Anemarrhena (知母) ground into powder, [taken] nine days [before delivery].

Scallion Porridge

Treats fetal stirring with spotting. Make porridge and add scallions, cook again, take on an empty stomach to calm abdominal pain. If there is bleeding from below and the fetus has died, the scallion white [will expel it].

Scallion White Decoction

Treats fetal stirring with spotting. Make a porridge, add scallions, cook, and take on an empty stomach to calm abdominal pain. If the fetus has died, scallion white will cause it to be expelled. Boil into a concentrated decoction and drink. If the fetus has died, scallion white will expel it.

Buddha's Hand Powder (Foshou San)

One Formula: An ancient remedy of divine efficacy. A formula using chicken. For treating fetal restlessness (threatened miscarriage) with abdominal pain and inability to swallow — this powder treats fetal agitation. Use pig's kidney, and in the remaining months use carp broth frequently. Take with rooster [preparations].

Another Formula: For a woman who cannot conceive, or when delivery is difficult — when the husband's cause leads to fetal movement and imminent labor, take a preparation ground to powder: one sheng of [ingredients], with gardenia (zhi zi), cattail pollen (pu huang), and other herbs to stop [bleeding] and stabilize. If the fetus descends, these substances transform and resolve the condition. The preparation also has the power to transform and bring results.

Another Formula for Miscarriage (Half-Birth / Premature Delivery):

When the fetal vine (placenta) falls — the fetal membranes descend — wind enters, the blood is pressed, a person may suffer injury to the branches [limbs]; if fire-illness is not yet corrected, then delivery occurs. This is the pattern of comparison: correct the core, and the major [problem] is resolved.

The source of the illness: fetal masses and wind — pulling at the sinews, so-called wind — becomes very severe and heavy, and there is no treatment. After the convulsions, one obtains the essential [medicine] and uses it in the comparison formula to correct and resolve.

If the fetal membranes are damaged and broken, the skin relaxes, remove the outer membrane; then the full placenta hidden below is obtained. For premature birth, one must add the corrective formula accordingly.

If the fetus is not properly positioned, or what is called in the fetal storehouse a rupture of the tissue — there are many treatments besides. Women recovering, raised in villages and towns, who have been given toxic herbal preparations — these folk practices have caused alarm, as is commonly seen.

translation:
White Hyacinth Bean Powder (白扁豆散) and Poria-Atractylodes Decoction (茯木湯): Formulas for preventing miscarriage and protecting the fetus during pregnancy.

White Hyacinth Bean Powder (白扁豆散):
For conditions of toxic blood failing to descend, rushing up to the heart causing confusion and agitation, and for counterflow qi attacking the heart, it is appropriate to take White Hyacinth Bean Powder. For those suffering from pathogenic wind invasion: one must first take this to resolve the condition.

During the fifth through seventh months of pregnancy, when yang qi is unstable, one must preventively take White Hyacinth Bean Powder to stabilize the pregnancy and prevent miscarriage and spotting.

At the half-month mark after the fifth through seventh months, if the fetus has not settled, one must take multiple doses of chrysanthemum decoction through the fourth month, then continue taking it thereafter until delivery.

For the formula: use one thousand gold pieces' worth of protective ingredients; seven to nine units of warming and fetal-stabilizing herbs; nine units of nourishing and harmonizing decoction to safely protect the fetus and calm it. Grind to powder. For sweating due to deficiency, take as powder without decoction.

For cases where the pregnancy is threatened: regulate and lightly drain downward; pour in ten doses; if there is counterflow to the heart with oral symptoms, take White Hyacinth Bean Powder to generate fluids and stop sweating.

Poria-Atractylodes Decoction (茯木湯):
Treats cases during the third, fourth, and fifth months when miscarriage is imminent and the patient is restless. Quickly decoct in water and take daily. One dose will settle the fetus and facilitate easy delivery, and aids in recovery after birth.

translation:
The formula uses prepared rehmannia (熟地) to nourish the fetus. Because it is non-toxic, it benefits pregnancy. Huang (astragalus/scutellaria) and the base herbs warm the fetus to nourish. It nourishes blood with white atractylodes, which moves and transforms dampness. When dampness is transformed, dryness is generated; when dryness and dampness are balanced, the fetus is stabilized.

Jin Gui An Tai Wan (Fetus-Stabilizing Pill from the Golden Cabinet)
Jin Gui Dang Gui San (Dang Gui Powder from the Golden Cabinet)
This formula is derived from the Golden Cabinet. The powder is appropriate to take to clear and disseminate. After blood deficiency is cleared of heat, this is suitable for those with a tendency toward slow or difficult delivery.

Take three qian each time. For pregnant women, dissolve in warm wine and take with dang gui, chuan xiong, bai zhu, huang qin, and wine-processed white herbs, which supplement and thus skillfully nourish blood; then poria...

The fetus-stabilizing medicinals: this formula contains dang gui to promote life and dry dampness. The ancients used it for both men and women — without toxic medicines, one may supplement the blood.

For dang gui, chuan xiong, lake-processed white (bai zhu), combined as a sage medicine: five liang, bai zhu, dampness, seven liang; the above [ingredients] as powder, each taken dissolved in a drink, one-two liang each; five right portions made into powder, each portion drunk separately...

Light circumstances: for preparing [a patient who] has blood [deficiency] — this cultivates and nourishes, supplements with bai zhu and dampness; the ancients used scutellaria (huang qin) along with clear white prepared wood to supplement.

Intelligence and wisdom, fatigue — not a false supplement: this medicine nourishes and thus this formula contains dang gui to produce life and dry dampness. Through repeated trials and verification, it is clear: during delivery, dang gui helps give birth to boys, chuan xiong without medicine is non-toxic and thus nourishes the blood.

Yu Wei An Tai Wan (Five-Flavor Fetus-Stabilizing Pill)
Dissolve in liquid and take; harmonize with seven pills; poria, pinellia, large white [atractylodes]; it is appropriate to take, each one liang, to nourish the blood, clear heat, with dang gui and chuan xiong.

translation:
궁귀보중탕 (Gung-gwi Bojung-tang / Xiong-gui Buzhong Decoction)

Treats pregnancy with qi and blood deficiency, weakness, and inability to nourish, leading to fetal bleeding/spotting. Ingredients include dried ginger and various herbs, each one qian; dried ginger with several flavors made into one dose with glue, applied as a point, decocted in water and taken. The five flavors include Angelica sinensis (Danggui), Atractylodes (Baizhu), Fragrant Angelica (Baizhi), Licorice (Gancao). One formula omits Costus root (Muxiang).

Anying Tang (Decoction to Calm and Nourish)

Treats unstable fetal qi with habitual miscarriage; suitable for prevention and stabilizing the fetus. Use 100 pills. White peony and other herbs, one liang each; Chuanxiong one liang; Angelica one liang; made into one dose. It addresses the Chong Mai meridian. Take monthly. Ingredients include glutinous rice, donkey-hide gelatin (Ejiao) pearls, Cyperus (Xiangfu), Mulberry mistletoe (Sangjisheng).

Qianjin Baotai Wan (Thousand Gold Fetus-Preserving Pills)

This formula nourishes the fetus; at the point of half-term miscarriage, one must absolutely restrict diet, cut off certain foods, and immediately support the yang qi, although the stomach meridian and blood supply may be insufficient. Ingredients: prepared Angelica washed in wine, ginger-fried Cyperus, processed with wine, vinegar, salt water, and Zhusha (cinnabar), prepared and formed into pills.

Two versions: one uses prepared Angelica, cooked Rehmannia (Shoudihuang) wine-fried, Cyperus processed with gelatin powder, salt water into pills.

Take with rice water. Chen Pi (tangerine peel) and other ingredients, 100 each, one qian; processed through the Pericardium meridian. Cinnabar two qian, half dried; each ground into powder one liang; with Chuanxiong, Mugwort leaf, mixed into pills, boiled with pepper.

translation:
Hwatongtang (Pain-Relieving Decoction)
Treats heart and abdominal pain after miscarriage. Ingredients: Danggwi (Angelica sinensis), Cheongung (Ligusticum chuanxiong), Baektaengnan (Lycopus), Hyangbu (Cyperus, dry-fried), Sukji (prepared Rehmannia) — each applied equally; Hwang (Scutellaria), each five fen; Doin (Peach kernel), Honghwa (Safflower) — each divided; per dose use eight fen with eight cups of water; add per cup: boys' urine and clear rice wine, each half a cup; decoct and take. If the medicine is not taken [as directed], [use] Alum as appropriate.

One formula: For women of forty or fifty years of age who become pregnant and wish to stabilize the fetus — chicken [broth], continuing through the eighth month; cook red herbs with millet into porridge and eat it accordingly.

One formula: Without using [strong] techniques, yet giving birth to twins in one day — for women with excessive ministerial fire in one to three months, left and right [sides], four [times] must [apply] — to prevent miscarriage, teach them to obtain a thick decoction of white [medicine] and cover [it].

Another formula: Same [as] pregnancy — regulate the woman's fetus, wonderful; use it to settle and stabilize the fetus, easily [prevents] miscarriage; otherwise [the fetus will] naturally fall.

Pulse Method (continued): When [the pulse] is slightly half [strength] up to the time of delivery, the monthly pulse is full; if [the pulse is] white-proper, the water belongs to [a state that is] the key to stabilizing the fetus. If [the pulse] becomes weak, then abdominal pain and blood appear within the abdomen; one immediately sees danger in delivery — be careful of injury.

Sudden Miscarriage: This occurs when a pregnant woman in the sixth or seventh month suddenly discharges more than a peck of water, and the fetus must gradually descend and be lost. When there is a sudden large discharge with much fluid, that is why [miscarriage occurs]. Uterine leakage means water slowly drips down, leading to miscarriage. This is how one knows it is a miscarriage.

translation:
Examining Color to Determine Life or Death of the Fetus

Signs to observe: If the mother's face is pale and her tongue is red with foam at the mouth, the child is dead but the mother will live. If the mother's face is red and her tongue is blue, the child is alive but the mother is in danger. If the lips are warm and the tongue is not blue, both mother and child live. If the face is blue and the tongue is red with froth at the mouth, with cold face during pregnancy, the fetus is dead. If the hands are blackened, the child is beyond saving. If the abdomen and navel area show pain connecting to the lower back, and the pulse is full, examine accordingly. If the fetus dies in the womb, the mother may survive while the child dies.

Signs of Impending Labor:
When the month arrives, the pregnant woman will feel the abdomen shift; or the navel area and abdomen become enlarged, with pulling sensations in the eyes and spine — these are signs of labor. When the pulse of a pregnant woman becomes irregular and she feels pain in the abdomen and around the navel, labor is near. Even if pain begins, if true labor has not commenced, do not sit on the birthing straw too early. If labor is not yet properly established, the abdomen and lower regions have not yet fully descended. Wait for the qi of the fetus to descend properly before proceeding. When the waist is heavy and there is pain, and the pulse is fine, use eye focus and strength — then birth will come.

Pulse Method:
When pain signals that delivery is near, this is the true sign of labor onset. The waist becomes heavy and sore, and strength is needed — this is when birth is imminent.

translation:
Protecting Childbirth (保產)

When the pulse at the wrist reaches three beats to the cycle and the channels separate — at midnight one feels pain, this is called "separation of the channels." Within one day it also counts as separation of the channels. When a woman is about to give birth urgently:

When the pulse is very fine and slippery at the chi position, with labor pains connecting through the lower back and abdomen, the membranes are about to rupture — this is a sign of imminent delivery. For women who have difficult labors, or who have reached nine or eight months, or who have had simple pregnancies — if the placenta and monthly cycle have internal irregularities, one must be cautious and cannot forcibly administer blood-quickening or labor-inducing medicines recklessly.

In cases where the fetus has difficulty, or a woman sits on the birthing mat too early before the months are complete — there are ancient formulas using herbs such as mugwort and other plants, administered as drinks to calm the fetus and prepare for delivery. The method and its applications have been transmitted by various masters.

The Purple Perilla Drink (紫蘇飲) is primarily [used for cases] of bitterness and difficulty. According to ancient formulas, if there is difficult labor, one may use this. Early physicians had their own enriching methods using Purple Perilla Drink to nourish and supplement after delivery, and also to use in combination with other formulas.

If a woman cannot turn over or move, or has been unable to stretch and endure great pain — one may use this formula, administering it to ease the body and allow safe delivery.

At nine months, if movement and stirring cause battle-like pains and the feet feel full, one may use methods to aid delivery as described. If there is abdominal bloating and qi stagnation, the Purple Perilla Drink should be administered.

One fears difficult labor: urgently administer Purple Perilla Drink. If one sees fullness and bloating in the abdomen with qi unable to move freely, administer accordingly and the delivery will proceed.

Throughout pregnancy the whole [body's] resources must be carefully managed. When one feels the water [breaking] and the months are complete, with blood and qi replete and spirit vigorous, the birth will proceed of its own accord.

translation:
Thinning the Fetus to Make Delivery Easy

The water that nourishes the child within the womb — if the fetal constitution is strong and robust, the membranes rupture slowly, breaking open, and then recede, so delivery is easy. For difficult labor, it is appropriate to use medicines that turn the fetus and promote delivery, such as: Yongyong-san, Shin Choisaeng-san, Huksan, Two Choisaeng-san, Three-san, Retreat Shin Pill, Flushing Blood-Down Breast-Blockage Retreat Scatter, Closed-Retreat Breast-Blockage Six-One Scatter, Bulsu-san, Retreat Scatter, Scatter to Release the Nine Dragon Scatter,令免飯龜散,扶葉丹, Two Retreat Choisaeng-san, Three Saeng Choisaeng, such as Yongyong-san, Shin-san, Black Scatter Two Choisaeng Three Scatter.

At the time of approaching delivery, if one is not careful to preserve the qi and blood, they will congeal and stagnate.

Concerning easy delivery: if purple mugwort grass is used at the time of sitting labor, it is appropriate to use it — at the time of delivery, remain upright and wait; when the pain spreads throughout, the birth passage opens, and delivery proceeds; one should administer the scatter medicines gradually.

Concerning easy delivery: if no progress is made day after day as delivery approaches, and delivery cannot occur, one should open [the passage] and dispel [the obstruction]; administer the Nine Dragon Scatter, 飯龜令家産散, gradually after delivery.

For sitting labor in difficult cases, the Bulsu-san, Choisaeng-san, Yongyong-san, Shin-san, Black Scatter, Two Choisaeng-san, Three-san are appropriate.

When the belt vessel is obstructed and cannot turn, and the woman's blood is deficient and overly weak, in the ninth or tenth month when the fetus is large and flourishing, this leads to congestion of qi and blood.

For easy delivery of a pregnant woman in seated labor, also for women in easy delivery — the mother should use the Nine[-month formula] to contract the fetal origin, then take the scatter; it will disperse naturally.

For delivery with Bulsu-san, the mother uses Nine to contract the fetal origin, then the scatter disperses naturally.

Ten Signs of Labor (十産侯)
The ten signs of labor: On day 1, normal labor; day 6, oblique presentation; day 2, sitting birth; day 3, rounded birth; day 4, prolapsed intestine birth; day 7, birth after fetal expulsion; suddenly the abdomen becomes tense, the child struggles to come out with difficulty on the road, unable to descend.

Normal Birth (正産)

Sitting Birth (坐産)

translation:
[Page 40 — On difficult and abnormal presentations in childbirth]

Normal delivery: The baby's head presents first (vertex presentation).

Supine birth (卧産):
This refers to the case where the mother lies on her back. Her birth canal lies flat, which requires a different approach so the body is not impeded.

Transverse presentation (横産):
This refers to a birth where a hand or arm appears first. Naturally, one must push it back. The treatment method is: make the mother lie on her back with her face upward, composing herself calmly, with her head supported properly.

One waits and watches; if the fingers appear first, the person gently and slowly pushes the limb back upward and corrects its position, guiding the hand back in, encouraging the child to come down properly. Push it back up gently, administer medicine, and use catalytic means to bring the baby down. Draw the hand back in carefully, raise it upward, and use an herbal ear [technique], correcting the head position.

Obstructed birth (遮産):
This refers to a birth where the mother has been straining with force, and the feet appear first (footling breech) — the baby has passed the normal birth position. If a hand or foot presents first — if both hands and feet present, or if it is a footling presentation — one uses a fine needle to stimulate [acupoints].

If the child is near and the obstruction involves the feet entering [the canal], causing one or two bouts of pain, then one or three times applies a poultice and needles the point, then applies a wash to the feet. Apply the treatment first, then ease [the child out gently].

If the mother's force came too early and caused alarm, apply a poultice, calm the child, correct the position; if the bowels have moved and there is urgency, act quickly.

The attendant, in approaching the case, should apply a beneficial warming poultice on the mother's abdomen; when the child is near, once the child's position is corrected, guide it gently, pushing the head back to correct orientation.

Oblique presentation (偏産):
This refers to a case where the baby is near but the head is tilted to one side, pressing against one side of the birth canal. Make the mother lie with head tilted back, guide the passage correctly, then use cloth bandaging and gentle pressure to assist.

translation:
Obstructed Labor (礙産):
When the mother lies on her back during birth and the child's two shoulders emerge, a person should gently push the child's shoulders upward, then gradually guide the child's body into proper alignment. Using force steadily, one hand guides [the child out]. If birth cannot be achieved, the treatment method is as follows: apply this method to enable delivery.

In mid-labor, because [the child's] upper [body] is stuck, the child is difficult to right. The birthing cord is already exposed and the child's shoulders are causing inability to deliver. The treatment method is to use [the appropriate technique] to enable birth.

Prolapsed Bowel Labor (盤腸産):
This refers to when, during childbirth, the pregnant woman's intestines prolapse before the child is delivered. After receiving the child, the intestines should immediately be treated. The treatment method is to wash with warm water and remove [residue], then use slightly warm water from grinding a knife blade to immediately reduce [the prolapse]. Another method: boil vinegar by half to induce reduction. Apply a headache-relieving plaster once; if the intestines cannot be fully reduced, have the mother lie on her back, and soothe her with words, or apply vinegar to the back — then the reduction will succeed.

Hot-season Labor (熱産):
In the depths of winter, when it is the height of summer heat, it is appropriate to keep the room tightly closed and screened, using water to cool a quiet room. Keep away from sunlight and drafts, and do not allow [the room] to be opened.

Cold-season Labor (凍産):
[In cold weather,] the atmosphere may still feel like spring or winter. It is appropriate to keep the lower body warm at all times and maintain warmth throughout, so as to prevent difficult labor.

One must carefully examine and determine whether the fetus is alive or dead before proceeding with treatment. If the fetus is dead, the tongue will change color and the abdomen will be distended and uncomfortable; use dispersing methods.

Sub-swelling (edema during pregnancy): When a pregnant woman has excessive water accumulation in the womb, around five or six months she will develop generalized body swelling. If the swelling does not cover the entire body...

[The condition involves] the skin becoming smooth. It is said that one must urgently use the Fangji (Stephania) decoction to address this. The kidneys are affected, and one uses Baimi (white rice) fish soup to nourish and disperse. The legs and feet swell, the face and muscles become puffy, the heart palpitates, reaching to the knees and ankles, the stomach and abdomen are affected. Add in cases of yellow water appearing, the body and limbs swell, and again using Fuling (Poria) relieves the swelling.

Zi Sou (Cough During Pregnancy)

When a pregnant woman develops a persistent cough that is difficult to stop, turning and becoming hard, this is called Zi Sou (pregnancy cough). The appropriate treatments are:

Ziyuan Decoction: Treats cough due to external wind-cold contracted during pregnancy. (Also: Madouling Powder and Tianmendong Drink.)
Ingredients: Ziyuan (purple aster root), Baihe (lily bulb), Tianmendong (asparagus root) — 2 qian each; Jiegeng (platycodon root) — 1 qian. Cut into one packet, add honey, half a cup of bamboo juice, simmer; add apricot kernels, boil, warm and take orally. Decoct, remove white skin; Gancao (licorice), Tianmendong — 1 qian each. Baihe Powder: Decoct in water. Treats cough. Jiegeng — 1 he, 1 qian; Ziyuan, Gancao — 5 fen; Beimu (fritillaria), Bai — one portion; Hu (pepper), apply ginger and red poria.

Madouling Powder: Treats pregnancy cough with wheezing and urgency. Chenpi (tangerine peel), Dafupi (areca husk), Sangbaipi (mulberry root bark), Renshen (ginseng), Bai Beimu (white fritillaria), [Ziyuan].
Wuweizi (schisandra), Jiegeng — 7 fen to 1 qian each; decoct with Madouling, Jiegeng, Renshen, Bai Beimu. Wuweizi, dried ginger — 3 slices; decoct half dose, cut and prepare.

Tianmendong Drink:
Wuweizi, Jiegeng, Ziyuan, Gancao, Zhimu (anemarrhena), Sangbaipi — 1 qian each. Cut into one packet, add water, decoct and take orally.

Treatment Methods

The scattered qi enters the various channels and cannot return to its origin, causing the mouth and nose to turn black, and foaming at the corners of the mouth and nose.

After childbirth, when a woman develops severe wheezing, it is extremely dangerous and close to death — the majority of such cases are fatal. Frequent childbirth leads to heavy blood loss; the defensive qi, after delivery, becomes deficient, leaving the lungs' qi in a state of acute wheezing and panting, which is alarming.

After childbirth, if severe wheezing develops and life is in danger, there is only a brief time to act. One should urgently administer a large dose of Xiong-Gui Powder (Cnidium-Angelica Powder) to stop this. Xuanfu Flower Decoction (旋覆花湯)

Eleven doses: Qianhu (Peucedanum), Perilla (Zisuye), Schizonepeta (Jingjie), Malt (Dongyou), Five-Flavor Berry (Wuweizi), Scutellaria (Huangqin), Red Poria (Chifuling), Red Peony (Chishaoyao).

Hiccups After Childbirth (咳逆)
Decoct three times and take warm after childbirth. For incessant hiccups to the point of near-death: two he of water, decoct with cinnamon bark (Rougui); add ginger juice three he, mix together, adjust dosage accordingly.

Inability to Speak After Childbirth (産後不語)
It is appropriate to use a dispersing formula to supplement the heart. When the patient first tries to speak no sound comes out, qi is exhausted and blocked, the condition has become cold, the tongue is stiff and speech is lost — in such cases Seven Jewels Formula (七珎散) or Lone Phoenix Powder (孤鳳散) is recommended.

Seven Jewels Powder (七珎散)
Decoct with water. Treats loss of speech after childbirth due to heart deficiency. Prevents wind and restores speech. Ingredients: Radix Ginseng (Sha Shen) and others, one qian each; Huangshi (Yellow Mineral), Acorus (Changpu), Ligusticum (Chuanxiong), each two fen; prepared thin.

Lone Phoenix Powder (孤鳳散)
Mint (He) one qian, decoct in water. Named for its formula to regulate. After childbirth, fine powder of pungent and sweet herbs difficult to list. Each dose one qian, taken eight times daily. Grind into fine powder, take with warm water to regulate stagnant blood and the menstrual channels.

Postpartum Hallucinations and Delirium (産後見鬼譫妄)
Suhexiang Pill (蘇合香元), one qian, dissolved in children's urine (Tongbian) and taken. This treats stagnant blood invading the heart and regulates the menstrual channels.

Treats postpartum heart deficiency with mental restlessness, disordered speech, and confused mind. Ingredients: Ginseng (人參), Angelica root (當歸).

Postpartum Fever
For severe cases remove heavy things; one must completely eliminate [the pathogen]; for lower abdominal [pain] in postpartum fever, it is appropriate to use [formulas with] Bupleurum (柴胡), adjusted as needed; Bupleurum is light and suitable for nighttime use.

Spirit-Blood Powder, Blood-Nourishing Decoction: for postpartum [conditions with] profuse lochia, disordered speech, fever from heat, use Cattle Gallstone (牛黄) paste, combined to treat alternating chills and fever; it is appropriate to use Bupleurum decoction.

Postpartum fever due to retained milk and stagnation: if one cannot fully resolve it, observe whether the milk flows freely — if milk flows on its own, it will heal; for pain, use [appropriate formulas to] disperse stagnation.

Bupleurum decoction, or Purple Bupleurum decoction, Rehmannia decoction, Schizonepeta decoction. For postpartum fever due to wind-cold, use Bupleurum and Rehmannia decoction.

For postpartum fever due to cold damage entering the blood chamber with breast pain: if the milk flows by itself it will heal; use Bupleurum decoction. For postpartum fever due to blood stasis, use Cooked Rehmannia Decoction (熟地黄湯).

King露散(Wang Lu San) — For promoting lactation (milk production):

Wang Lu San: Used for cold-pattern conditions, to bring down breast milk. Ingredients: Platycodon (Jiegeng), Poria (Fuling), Ligusticum (Chuanxiong), Angelica dahurica (Baizhi) — 1 qian each; Angelica sinensis (Danggui), Red Peony (Chishao) — 2 qian each.

Pig's Trotter Porridge: Take four pairs of pig's trotters, prepare as for eating. Add 3 dou of water and boil down to 1 dou. Remove the trotters. Add scallion, Wang Gua (snake gourd), Tongcao (rice paper plant), and Loulu (rhaponticum) — 3 liang each. Boil again to get 3 sheng. Make into porridge and eat.

One Formula: Take rice and boil to get 6 sheng of liquid. Remove the rice, make a gruel with scallion, fermented soybeans, Wang Gua root, Tongcao, and Loulu — right amounts. Boil again and consume one cupful. Effective. Grind fine and mix with water.

Another Formula: Using red [herb], to bring down milk: take 1 qian of licorice powder and one measure of scallion, decoct and take finely ground. Effective.

Another Formula: At the start of lactation when there is no milk, use winter bean powder (2 parts), add licorice powder 1 qian, decoct with scallion, one cup, take warm.

Third Formula: When there is no milk, add much lard [illegible quantities], take with warm wine daily.

Postpartum prolapse of the vaginal walls: After childbirth if the vaginal walls protrude due to excessive straining during labor, use scallion decoction with Danggui (Angelica) — fumigate and wash the affected area.

Section: Overdue Birth (過月不產)

Regarding pregnancies that go past the expected month without delivery — the reason for this lies in the following: normally the fetus completes its development through the menstrual cycle, and some pregnancies extend beyond the expected term by three to five portions. If the monthly blood normally nourishes the uterus fully, the fetus will be well-nourished, but when delivery is delayed, it is because there is surplus blood. Even though the fetus moves, the meridians still have blood descending monthly, yet the blood itself has not been damaged — the uterus is abundantly nourishing the child, which is why birth is delayed.

In cases where delivery is difficult and prolonged past nine or ten months, it is often seen that after two or three such difficult births, the patient may vomit or bleed, and the blood below the seventh month has not been damaged. The uterus remains well-nourished, and so the pregnancy continues until the fourth or fifth month without delivery. The difficulty arises because tonifying medicines for qi and blood deficiency are hard to use to extend this further.

Take amomum fruit (縮砂) and perilla leaf (紫蘇葉), decoct in water, and take — delivery will follow promptly. One may also add cyperus root, peach kernel, and other such herbs. For overdue pregnancy without delivery, use the Four Yang formula accordingly.

translation:
Yimo Pill (Leonurus Pills)
Contains Leonurus (motherwort) pills, also known as a nourishing compound formula, able to regulate yin, nourish life-force, and treat all manner of diseases before and after childbirth, including difficult labor. It can also activate blood circulation and regulate qi.

Yimo Ointment (Leonurus Ointment)
Commonly known as Leonurus grass ointment; it can treat various diseases of women in childbirth, including assisting delivery when the birth is obstructed, with miraculous effects. Also:

[For conditions of weight and fullness:] Treats cases where [the fetus] has encroached and is not moving, facilitating delivery in various diseases of pregnant women who cannot deliver, bringing out the spirit and effectiveness. Take [the herb], prepare with silver and stone instruments, and take together with Leonurus.

To stop or terminate pregnancy:
Decoct a soup for women to regulate the uterus; while it is still empty, protect and regulate with Achyranthes (Niuxi) soaked in wine, taken as a gelatin decoction. After childbirth, this may be taken in small amounts. Related to the Four Substances (Si Wu) formula.

[For uterine masses in women:] Because of disease, remove [the obstruction from] the womb; in three doses, the feet will feel it and it can be expelled downward. Formula: two liang of malt (Maiya), Chuanxiong, and Shaoyao with large amounts of Shen.

[For fermented grain formulas:] For women with uterine masses, use half a sheng, blend and decocted, apply and take. After three doses the feet will respond and the condition can be expelled downward. Good formula. Also: two liang of radish seed (Laifuzi) with Shen.

In the fifth month, take five sheng, process into a paste, dry and take daily. Every month, the fermented grain is steeped in good wine, consumed monthly; then strain and decoct down to two sheng, take half [a sheng] each time, following the seed-removal method.

On the fifth day, strain out the white, remove the fermented grain, grind to powder, blend and decoct, apply and take. After three doses the feet will respond and the condition can be expelled. Good formula. Also: two liang of radish seed with Shen.
○ Another formula: burn a piece of paper in the shape of a round pill, have [the woman] take it burned; this method will permanently stop [future] pregnancies.

translation:
Diseases of Widows and Buddhist Nuns, Different from Those of Wives and Concubines

Take on an empty stomach as if one were not with child. A separate preparation method for the yin (reproductive) condition of widows.

[The text discusses] women of full constitution who have desires but suffer from heat-related conditions of deficiency taxation. Because they cannot fulfill their desires, they accumulate pathogenic heat. As recorded in the medical case histories of Chunyu Yi (Cang Gong), this results from the conflict of yin and yang forces, generating cold and heat patterns.

When the pulse is wiry, this indicates that a man's essence is involved — this is how the diagnosis is made. The condition presents with alternating cold and heat. Cang Gong diagnosed it by examining the liver pulse.

A wiry pulse in a woman indicates suppressed desires; because she lives alone without a husband, heat accumulates in the liver. The medical records of Cang Gong describe this liver pulse presentation as indicating disease.

[Symptoms include:] fatigue, a wiry pulse, feverish sensations in the face, redness of the face, pain in the flanks and abdomen, mental restlessness, palpitations, and disturbed menstruation.

This condition arises because the woman's will and spirit cannot be fulfilled. The appropriate treatment is to regulate and move the menses, to calm the spirit.

[In terms of prescriptions:] decoct and take the medicine; one may add Ginseng (Renshen), Poria with Pine Root (Fushen), Aconite (Fuzi), or other herbs to nourish and supplement.

For those who are thin and pale with a haggard complexion, it is appropriate to use formulas that nourish the spirit, such as Huangqi Tang (Astragalus Decoction) and similar preparations.

translation:
Miscellaneous Diseases of Women

Women who suffer from stagnant or retained qi, and those who are prone to brooding — their minds become sites of accumulation [of pathological influences]. They frequently dwell in dampness. From age fifteen onward, as yin water [menses] begins, one can fully discuss their condition. The intercourse of women leads to separate diseases; one must establish separate formulas. The pathways of stored qi become cut off externally; the blood fails to be regulated, harming the gallbladder and causing collapse. As for childbirth,崩漏 (flooding and spotting), grief, sorrow, and excessive worry — these all differ. Looking at nine key areas of hardness, women's emotional illnesses multiply. Adding ten roots of worry and difficulty, the illness goes deep. For treatment, it is appropriate to supplement the nine types of qi. The Qi-Dispersing Powder (散) is unable to detail [all conditions]; one traces the origin of life processes. For disorders of the head and blood, the three diseases of ten roots of deep worry apply. It is appropriate to use the Nine-Supplement Decoction, the Earth-Yellow Pill (Dihuang Wan), the Spirit-Nourishing Chuanxiong Formula, the Far-Reaching Dispersing Powder, and for flooding and fullness, use [formulas to regulate] blood overflow and abdominal fullness. For each attachment, nourish and moisten; reach the yin; use the Spirit-Calming Decoction to supplement and drain; for sweating and dryness, use Citrus (橘) formulas. For no sweating: fragrant herb, two liang; aconite (fuzi), four liang; tangerine peel, two liang; poria, licorice root, each to amount.

Qi-Suppressing Powder (抑氣散)
[Ingredients as listed: aromatic herbs, prepared as one packet, with jujube dates and licorice root decocted in water.]

Exotic Fragrance Four-Spirit Powder (異香四神散)
[Ingredients as listed: aromatic herbs, prepared as one packet, with jujube dates, cinnamon twig, and licorice root decocted in water.]

[This page from Dongui Bogam describes several medical conditions and treatments for newborn infants (小兒, "small children/infants"). The text is partially damaged and some columns are difficult to read in full. The following is a best-effort translation of the legible content:]

Pediatric Conditions — General:

[Column 1 — Fire/Charcoal Qi entering the abdomen]: When charcoal qi enters the abdomen, causing the condition to recur, use a large paper twist soaked in hot vinegar to warm-wash the pus-cord. This causes the qi to return and breathing to be restored, so that fainting ceases.

[Column 2 — Newborn with white, blue, purple discoloration]: For a newborn infant, the standard method is to immediately use white silkworm, purple cinnamon, aged tangerine peel, and licorice root, each five portions, burned with moxa, to restore the qi and breathing.

[Column 3 — Evil blood entering the mouth at birth]: If at birth evil blood enters the infant's mouth and the child appears to be dying, urgently examine the child's mouth — if there is a swelling or membrane blocking the airway above, with blisters, break it with a finger and remove the blood with silk cloth, wiping away the obstruction.

[Column 4 — Similar condition, repeated treatment]: If at birth evil blood enters the mouth and death seems imminent, urgently look into the infant's mouth; if there is a raised membrane, insert a finger to break it, remove the blood with cloth, and wipe it away.

[Column 5 — Neonatal condition treated with ink and herbs]: Rub ink inside the mouth, then apply a decoction of agastache and peppermint; do not nurse for one hour. This is called "horse teeth" (馬牙). If untreated, it will worsen.

[Column 6 — Neonatal birthmarks/spots and treatment with honey]: For birthmarks or spots appearing on a newborn, treat the area with honey; after about one hour the condition should resolve.

[Column 7 — Treatment with Suhap fragrant pills]: For newborns [with a certain condition], apply a small amount of Suhap Hyang-won (蘇合香元) to the relevant point, using it like a golden jade sound needle at the indicated location.

translation:
Treatments for newborns and infants — various remedies:

[General heading:] If the newborn cannot be given milk by mouth, take a paper wick, light it, and continue; do not use a small vessel; pour into a large cup; use Coptis (Huanglian) and Gardenia (Zhizi) decoction.

Newborn infants: Use Poria (Fuling); if unable to take silver vessel [feeding], insert into the mouth; use eight mouthfuls; adjust with one dose of nine pellets the size of a Chinese parasol seed.

Newborn infants: Use a decoction; pour into the mouth through the wooden [tube]; ginger powder with honey, nine pills the size of a parasol seed.

Newborn infants with failure to pass urine and stool: the abdomen becomes distended, the heart [chest] area and lower abdomen are urgent; have a woman warm the area with her hands to help the child.

[Milk treatment:] Take mother's milk; mix in two portions; if the child does not improve after several applications, take the juice; mix red and white milk juice in equal halves and adjust the dosage.

Newborn with blocked stool: urgently use fresh earthworms (Dilong), several pieces, with cinnabar (Zhusha) and borneol (Longnaо), grind together.

Newborn: Use fumigation with fragrant herbs decoction, adjusted with a little Ophiopogon (Maidong); burn inner paper ash; use cinnabar and borneol ground together.

Infant downward-moving formula: Use cinnabar pills — cinnabar with red Arisaema (Nanxing), roasted, with Cardamom (Doukou) and other ingredients in appropriate proportions, taken orally.

translation:
[Right side, main column:]
Decoct into a soup and pour down. Pills of paste. Two to nine doses of powder. Drink immediately. Take red centipede — two pieces, remove head and feet, roast until charred, grind, add bamboo sap, mix until smooth.

[Column: Infant — Thrush (Mouth)]
For a newborn infant with thrush (white coating in the mouth): Use powdered medicine, divide into two doses. Wipe the inside of the mouth repeatedly with a finger wrapped in silk cotton dampened with ginger juice until the white patches are gone. If the infant cannot suckle milk, mix with milk water and administer. The mouth resembles a goose's mouth — treat urgently.

Mix powder evenly, divide into portions with jade [a fine quality preparation], two portions, pour into mouth.

[Column: Infant — Internal treatment]
For a newborn infant: Use dragon [borneol/dragon brain] inside. Wipe the inside of the mouth with a finger wrapped in silk dampened with ginger juice. Wait until the juice [takes effect]; if not resolved, combine with China-root water, wipe and contend with the condition if the mouth does not respond urgently. Licorice root (one portion). Another formula: Dragon brain (borneol), one fen. Small amounts.

[Column: Burning/Scorching treatment]
Burn, take the juice in a cup, apply. Also apply white willow branch spirits. Apply to the affected area.

[Column: Infant — Body rash at birth]
For a newborn infant: Apply lead powder (minium) mixed with rice flour all over the body, rub in. Do so when the skin shows no redness yet but the flesh beneath is red.

[Column: Infant — Nasal congestion]
For a newborn infant with nasal congestion and inability to pass through: The infant cannot feed because of this. Take Suhe (Storax) pill with water. See [formula for] horn and grass, crow [ingredients], and Arisaema (天南星).

[Column: Infant — Poultice for fontanelle]
Mix with star [herb], apply as poultice to the chin and fontanelle area. Grind to powder, mix with paste, apply to the chin and fontanelle. Also [another method follows].
